g1.label: 1. If the temperature ___ below minus 20 (Type 1)
g1.why: Type 1 keeps the present simple after “if”, even though the main clause uses “will”.

g2.label: 2. If I ___ in Quebec (Type 2)
g2.why: Type 2 uses the past simple after “if” for an imagined, unreal situation.

g3.label: 3. …if the weather ___ warmer (Type 1)
g3.why: Type 1: present simple after “if” — “gets”, never “will get”.

g4.label: 4. If we ___ Indigenous languages (Type 1)
g4.why: Type 1 needs a present-simple negative after “if”: "don't protect".

g5.label: 5. If Canada ___ a smaller country (Type 2)
g5.why: Type 2 uses “were” for every person in this unreal condition.

g6.label: 6. …if the government ___ better roads (Type 1)
g6.why: Type 1: present simple after “if”, with third-person -s on “builds”.

g7.label: 7. If you ___ visit any Canadian city (Type 2)
g7.why: Type 2 uses “could” here to mean “if it were possible”.

g8.label: 8. If more young people ___ Inuktitut (Type 2)
g8.why: Type 2 uses the past simple after “if” — the situation is imagined, not real.
